description.en: SPINE evaluates LLM sycophancy by having an adaptive LLM proxy persistently challenge a target model across up to 25 turns on false-presupposition and unethical-query items, measuring collapse rates.

evaluationEvidence.scoring: Our experimental results show that collapse rates increase with conversation length for every model, short-horizon protocols underestimate sycophancy and resistance under sustained pressure remains unreliable across current models.
evaluationEvidence.task: We introduce SPINE, a benchmark in which an LLM proxy plays a persistent but mistaken user and adaptively challenges a target model for up to 25 turns. We evaluate four production systems and three Olmo3-7b variants on 100 false-presupposition and 100 unethical-query items.

claire_radar.motivation: Large language models (LLMs) may abandon correct positions when users push back, exhibiting a failure mode known as sycophancy.
